elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "The access and rights to use provided to the Company under this Section 1.4 shall extend to the Company's affiliates upon written notice to HDI." Coverage is conditioned on notice, which satisfies the extension at the fallback threshold and, in substance, extends the grant to affiliates.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 1.4 as rendered nor the inserted sentence mentions contractors or agents acting on the Company's behalf; the extension names only "the Company's affiliates".
No perpetuity language anywhere in the rendered grant; Section 1.4 is a service-access right with no stated term, and no clause states that fully paid rights survive perpetually.
The word "irrevocable" (or equivalent) does not appear; while there is no at-will revocation by HDI, the absence of revocation language is not an affirmative irrevocability grant.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The rationale itself concedes the only exit is the mutual 90-day termination right in Section 4.1, i.e. termination for convenience; the redline does not restrict termination of the access rights to uncured material breach, and Section 4.1 is not amended.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 10.3: the Agreement "shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns" — the rights carry to our successors and assigns with no assignment consent gate.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted operative sentence expressly extends the Section 1.4 access and use rights to "the Company's affiliates upon written notice to HDI" — trigger (written notice to HDI) and scope (Section 1.4 access and use rights) are both defined.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: Section 10.3 (unamended, favourable existing language) makes the Agreement enforceable by and inure to the benefit of the parties' "successors and assigns" with no anti-assignment restriction, which reaches an M&A successor.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single inserted sentence supplies affiliate coverage on written notice, and retained Section 10.3 already carries the rights to successors and assigns, so no further edit is required to land at the fallback.

Preferred level fails on four elements the drafter deliberately did not pursue: contractors acting on our behalf are absent, there is no perpetual or irrevocable paid-up formulation, and termination of the access rights remains available under the Section 4.1 90-day convenience right rather than being limited to uncured material breach.

Minimality holds: exactly one sentence was added, it is scoped to Section 1.4, it uses the same access/right-to-use vocabulary as the existing grant, and it adds no survival tail, expense allocation, procedure, or other extra beyond the affiliate element.

Intent is preserved: bandwidth, burst-capacity, catalog-monitoring purpose, the Section 4.1 termination mechanic and the Section 10.3 assignment allocation all survive unchanged, and the insertion leaves no dangling cross-reference ("Section 1.4" is the clause it sits in).

Drafting note, not a defect for this level: Section 10.3's tail "but no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement" sits in tension with affiliate use. The insertion is framed as extending HDI's obligation to the Company's affiliates rather than granting affiliates enforceable rights, so it is not contradictory, but adding "except as provided in Section 1.4" to Section 10.3 would remove any argument that affiliate access is barred.

Second drafting note: "affiliates" is used in lower case and is not a defined term in the Agreement; this is workable on plain meaning, but if the counterparty pushes back, define Affiliate rather than leaving scope to argument.
